svg.title: Refresh Token Rotation
svg.desc: Refresh Token Rotation. Short-lived access tokens, single-use refresh tokens, and reuse detection that revokes the whole family. Step 1, Short-lived access token: The app calls the API with a 10-minute access token. Once it expires, the API answers 401. Step 2, Refresh and rotate: The app sends RT1 to the token endpoint and gets a new access token plus RT2. RT1 is now used. Step 3, Reuse is detected: An attacker replays a stolen copy of RT1. Already used: the server revokes the whole family. Step 4, Sign in again: RT2 was revoked too, so the app gets invalid_grant. The user signs in again: a new family starts.

g.text: The app calls the API with a 10-minute access token. Once it expires, the API answers 401.
The app sends RT1 to the token endpoint and gets a new access token plus RT2. RT1 is now used.
An attacker replays a stolen copy of RT1. Already used: the server revokes the whole family.
RT2 was revoked too, so the app gets invalid_grant. The user signs in again: a new family starts.

g.text: A refresh token arrives. It is…
mark it used, issue the next
Sign-in started this family; RT1 is its first refresh token.
The server keeps a family ID, a hash of each token and its status.
RT1 arrives and is still active, so the refresh goes through.
RT1 becomes used and RT2 joins the family: each refresh token works once.
RT1 arrives a second time. It was already used: that is reuse.
Thief or app? The server can't tell, so it revokes the whole family.
RT2 was revoked with its family, so the app has to sign the user in again.
A new family starts. At most, a thief keeps an access token for minutes.
then the user signs in again.
stole a copy of RT1 earlier
its RT1 died with the old family
